title: Advice that stops at the doorstep
odia: କହି ଦେଉଥାଇ ପରକୁ, ବୁଦ୍ଧି ନ ଦିଶଇ ଘରକୁ
literal_meaning: One keeps advising others, but wisdom is not seen at home.
explanation: The criticism is the gap between giving advice and practising it. The outward-facing adviser appears wise, yet fails to apply that wisdom to their own affairs. The saying invites self-examination; it does not imply that advice is worthless whenever its giver has difficulties.
meaning_odia: ଅନ୍ୟକୁ ଉପଦେଶ ଦେଇ ନିଜେ ତାହା ନ ମାନିବା।
usage_example: A person lectures everyone about keeping accounts but repeatedly loses track of their own spending. A relative uses this line to point out the inconsistency. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The rhyme of ପରକୁ and ଘରକୁ reinforces the contrast between others and home. Here the structure is part of the saying’s force, not just decoration.
